title: Textbook Spine / Part IV: Lower Bounds

definitions.name: Worst-case and minimax expected regret
definitions.fallback: The minimax value is the infimum over policies of their worst expected regret over the environment class.

definitions.name: Least-explored alternative
definitions.fallback: Among the m alternatives, at least one is pulled no more than the average n divided by m.

definitions.name: Two-environment algebra
definitions.fallback: A quantitative upper bound on the pull-count discrepancy leaves a matching error term in the two-environment regret lower bound.

steps.title: Choose the base instance
steps.detail: Give arm zero mean Delta and every alternative mean zero.

steps.title: Find a lightly sampled alternative
steps.detail: Use the expected pull budget to choose i.succ with expected count at most n/m.

steps.title: Change one source
steps.detail: Raise only that alternative mean to 2 Delta; keep the policy fixed.

steps.title: Write both regret expressions

steps.detail: A same-policy history-law KL/change-of-measure theorem must supply a quantitative pull-count discrepancy error before the minimax conclusion can follow.

source_theorem.label: Theorem 13.1 (source statement; proof deferred to Chapter 15)
source_theorem.math: \exists c>0\;\forall k>1\;\forall n\ge k:\quad R_n^*(\mathcal E^k)\ge c\sqrt{kn},
source_theorem.fallback: For unit-variance k-armed Gaussian bandits with means in the unit cube, minimax regret is at least a universal constant times the square root of k times n.
source_theorem.plain: The source states the finite-arm Gaussian minimax order here and explicitly postpones its proof to Chapter 15.

chapters.title: Foundations of Information Theory
chapters.status_note: The source-faithful §14.2 relative-entropy and Bretagnolle–Huber spine is compiled. Entropy/source coding in §14.1 and full sub-sigma-algebra data processing remain outside this scoped gate.

§14.2 Relative Entropy (printed pp. 188–191 / PDF pp. 197–200; formal target window)
learning_goals: Read relative entropy as an extended-real, direction-sensitive comparison of probability measures.
Distinguish the absolutely-continuous log-likelihood branch from singular support mismatch.
Map a measurable event to Bernoulli probabilities without increasing KL.
Derive the unconditional Bretagnolle–Huber testing bound, including the exp(-infinity)=0 branch.
Keep general coding theory and adaptive bandit-history decomposition outside the compiled §14.2 window.

definitions.name: Entropy and optimal coding
definitions.fallback: Entropy is the expected information content of a discrete outcome and motivates the chapter's coding discussion.

definitions.name: Extended-real relative entropy
definitions.math: D(P\Vert Q)=\int \log\!\left(\frac{dP}{dQ}\right)dP,\qquad D(P\Vert Q)=+\infty\text{ if }P\not\ll Q.
definitions.fallback: Relative entropy is the expected log likelihood ratio when P is absolutely continuous with respect to Q, and infinity on support mismatch.

definitions.name: Bernoulli relative entropy
definitions.fallback: The two-point specialization uses zero-mass terms equal to zero and infinity when P assigns positive mass where Q assigns none.

definitions.name: Bretagnolle–Huber testing scale
definitions.fallback: The real-valued scale makes the source convention exponential of negative infinity equals zero explicit.

steps.title: Split the KL branches
steps.detail: Use Mathlib's exact absolute-continuity and log-likelihood integrability characterization; retain infinity on support mismatch.

steps.title: Coarsen to one event
steps.detail: Restrict both measures to A and its complement and prove d(P(A),Q(A)) is at most D(P,Q).

steps.title: Prove the binary bound
steps.detail: Lower-bound binary likelihood affinity by exp(-d/2), then compare squared affinity with the two testing errors.

steps.title: Restore all endpoints
steps.detail: Handle Bernoulli zero/one support cases through the extended-real endpoint convention.

steps.title: Lift to measures
steps.detail: Use antitonicity of the testing scale and Q(A complement)=1-Q(A) to obtain the source theorem in the P-to-Q KL direction.

source_theorem.label: Theorem 14.2 / Eq. (14.7) (Bretagnolle–Huber)
source_theorem.fallback: For two probability measures and any measurable event, the sum of the P error on A and the Q error on its complement is at least one half times exponential negative relative entropy.
source_theorem.plain: Observing an event cannot make two laws easier to distinguish than their full relative entropy permits.
source_theorem.boundary: BanditRLProof.LowerBounds.bretagnolleHuber compiles this unconditional measure/event theorem with D(P,Q), Q(A complement), and an explicit zero scale at infinite KL. It does not claim §14.1 source coding, full Exercise 14.10, or the Chapter 15 adaptive-history chain rule.

definitions.name: Bandit-history divergence
definitions.fallback: The divergence compares n-round action/reward histories generated by the same possibly randomized policy in two environments.

definitions.name: Unit-variance Gaussian arm
definitions.fallback: Each arm is a real Gaussian probability law with the requested mean and variance exactly one.

definitions.name: Equal-variance Gaussian KL
definitions.fallback: The relative entropy between unit-variance Gaussians is one half the squared difference of their means.

definitions.name: Source minimax gap
definitions.fallback: The tuned gap makes the information exponent exactly one half and is at most one half when k-1 is at most n.

steps.title: Choose the base instance
steps.detail: Set the first Gaussian mean to Delta and all other means to zero.

steps.title: Find a least-explored alternative
steps.detail: Use the compiled Chapter 13 averaging leaf to choose i>1 with E[T_i(n)] at most n/(k-1).

steps.title: Change one arm
steps.detail: Raise only arm i to mean 2 Delta; its compiled arm-level KL cost is 2 Delta squared.

steps.title: Lift KL to histories
steps.detail: Lemma 15.1 must turn arm costs into the first-law expected pull-count sum under one common stochastic policy; this node is blocked.

steps.title: Test and tune
steps.detail: Apply Chapter 14 Bretagnolle–Huber to T_1(n) at most n/2, then choose Delta=sqrt((k-1)/(4n)) to obtain the 1/27 lower bound; the terminal remains blocked with its dependency.

source_theorem.label: Lemma 15.1 / Eq. (15.1) and Theorem 15.2
source_theorem.fallback: History KL is the first-law expected sum of arm KL costs under one common policy; the Gaussian construction then yields regret at least one twenty-seventh times the square root of (k-1)n.
source_theorem.plain: The theorem converts indistinguishability of one-coordinate Gaussian alternatives into a finite-arm minimax regret obstruction.
source_theorem.boundary: Only the Gaussian arm constructor, log likelihood ratio, integrability, and exact arm-level KL currently compile. Lemma 15.1 and Theorem 15.2 are not local proofs: Mathlib lacks the needed conditional-KL integral, and the current repository policy interface is deterministic rather than the source's randomized policy kernel.
